name: Hydroxycarbamide
drug_class: Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor (antimetabolite); fetal haemoglobin inducer
route_note: oral capsules, tablets or solution once daily
originator: Squibb (antineoplastic development); first synthesised by Dresler and Stein
owner: generic (many); Bristol Myers Squibb (Hydrea, Droxia); Theravia (Siklos)

discovery.by: W. F. C. Dresler and R. Stein
discovery.note: First synthesised in Germany; its antileukaemic activity was recognised in the 1960s.

tagline: Old antimetabolite that became the backbone of sickle cell disease treatment
summary: Hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea) inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, slowing DNA synthesis. It is used for myeloproliferative neoplasms and some cancers, and since the 1990s it has been the main disease-modifying therapy for sickle cell anaemia, where it raises fetal haemoglobin and reduces painful crises.
mechanism: Hydroxycarbamide quenches the tyrosyl free radical in the R2 subunit of ribonucleotide reductase, blocking conversion of ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides. This arrests cells in S phase and is cytotoxic to rapidly dividing cells.

In sickle cell disease it increases fetal haemoglobin (HbF), which inhibits polymerisation of HbS, possibly through stress erythropoiesis and nitric oxide release. It also lowers neutrophil and reticulocyte counts and reduces red cell adhesion to endothelium.
uses: Sickle cell anaemia with recurrent painful crises (adults and children)
Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with radiation
Polycythaemia vera and essential thrombocythaemia (common use; labelled in some countries)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Hydrea for cancer treatment.

history.title: HbF induction
history.detail: Small studies show hydroxyurea raises fetal haemoglobin in sickle cell patients.

history.title: MSH trial
history.detail: The Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea is stopped early after showing about 50% fewer painful crises.

history.title: Droxia
history.detail: FDA approves hydroxyurea (Droxia) for adults with sickle cell anaemia.

history.title: BABY HUG
history.detail: Trial in infants shows fewer painful crises and dactylitis.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: FDA approves Siklos for children aged two years and older with sickle cell anaemia.

pk.metabolism: partly hepatic and by urease of gut bacteria

safety.boxed_warning: Droxia and Siklos labels: myelosuppression may be severe and life-threatening; hydroxyurea is carcinogenic, and secondary leukaemia and skin cancer have been reported.

facts: WHO lists hydroxycarbamide both as a cytotoxic medicine and as a medicine for sickle cell disease.
